title: Momentum Distribution and Contact Parameters of a mass-imbalanced three-body system across the Efimov-Unatomic transition
authors: D. S. Rosa, R. M. Francisco, T. Frederico, G. Krein, M. T. Yamashita
abstract: We investigate the single-particle momentum distribution and contact parameters of mass-imbalanced three-body systems at the critical dimension Dc, where the transition between discrete and continuous scale invariance takes place as the spatial dimension is tuned between three and two dimensions. We show that the asymptotic momentum distribution at Dc is governed by a distinct logarithmic scaling structure, which differs fundamentally from both the log-periodic behavior of Efimov states and the power-law scaling of the unatomic regime. This structure requires the introduction of an additional three-body contact parameter associated with a quadratic logarithmic contribution, leading to a finite and well-defined description of the momentum tail at the transition. This additional three-body parameter depends sensitively on the mass imbalance, changing sign across different mass configurations and vanishing for identical particles. As a consequence, the three-body contribution to the momentum distribution can be suppressed at a characteristic momentum scale, leaving the asymptotic tail entirely determined by the two-body contact. We further analyze the narrow intermediate region connecting the Efimov and unatomic regimes, here identified as an intermediate scaling regime, whose extent and properties are strongly controlled by the mass ratio. These results establish the critical dimension as a regime with emergent scaling properties and provide experimentally accessible signatures for probing the transition between discrete and continuous scale invariance in few-body quantum systems.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes three-body quantum systems across the dimensional transition between Efimov and unatomic regimes. It finds that at the critical dimension, the system's momentum tail requires a unique logarithmic scaling structure governed by an additional three-body contact parameter. This work establishes the critical dimension as a key point for probing emergent scaling properties in few-body quantum gases.
main_problem: The study investigates how the momentum distribution and contact parameters of a mass-imbalanced three-body quantum system evolve as the spatial dimension is tuned across the critical point separating Efimov and unatomic regimes.
main_result: At the critical dimension, the asymptotic momentum tail exhibits a unique logarithmic scaling structure requiring an additional three-body contact parameter, which can lead to the suppression of the three-body contribution at finite momenta.
method: The authors use theoretical methods involving solving Faddeev equations in an effective noninteger spatial dimension D and analyzing the large-momentum asymptotic behavior of the spectator function.
model_or_system: The model is a mass-imbalanced three-body quantum system, analyzed by mapping its physics onto an effective continuous spatial dimension D, allowing for a dimensional crossover between different physical regimes.
key_observables: Single-particle momentum distribution (large-momentum tail), two-body contact parameter ($C_2$), and the newly introduced three-body contact parameter ($C''_3$).
important_parameters: The critical dimension $D_c$, the mass imbalance ratio, and the intermediate scaling regime width $\Delta = D_c - D$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system to an effective noninteger spatial dimension D and using asymptotic expansions for momentum space functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scaling parameter $s_n$ vs. dimension D across Efimov, critical, and unatomic regimes; another figure quantifies the width of the intermediate scaling regime dependence on mass imbalance; a third shows the logarithmic asymptotic form at $D_c$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system's behavior in three distinct dimensional regimes (Efimov, Unatomic, Intermediate) by deriving the momentum distribution components and identifying the necessary contact parameters required to maintain physical consistency across the transition point.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding how fundamental many-body physics transitions between different scaling laws (log-periodic vs. power-law) in ultracold atomic systems, offering new experimental signatures based on momentum measurements.

Upper panel: Full behavior for the 23Na2 – 40K system, show- ing the Efimov regime (sn = ±is0) for D > Dc, the critical di- mension Dc (black point), and the transition to real solutions below it. The green point marks D, below which the asymp- totic behavior of the momentum distribution is entirely gov- erned by a three-body contribution exhibiting power-law scal- ing, characteristic of the unatomic regime. FIG. 2. Difference Dc −D, which defines the width of the Scale Invariant Regime (SIR), as a function of the mass ratio mB/mA. The SIR corresponds to the interval in dimension where the system is not described by either Efimov (discrete scaling) or unatomic (continuous scaling) regimes. The highlighted points indicate experimentally rel- evant heavy–heavy–light mixtures: 133Cs2 – 6Li, 41K2 – 6Li, and 23Na2 – 40K. As the mass imbalance increases, the width of the SIR decreases, indicating that the crossover between discrete and continuous scale invariance becomes increasingly localized in dimension.
